summary:
Last night in a dream my ex tomcat Horny Ernie appeared to me saying, “You better write Mrs. Le Guin now that you’re over pneumonia, or she’ll think you didn’t like her book.” He then vanished in a cloud of fleas or whatever it is he does to get out of there fast. 

I haven’t written, you see, because I almost croaked. First I had (do you care? Does anyone care? If so why didn’t they come by while I was lying there in my bed week after week?) the London flu and then strep throat and then pneu­ monia and after that I didn’t feel too good and stayed home a lot. This started in Nov and ended about two weeks ago when Tessa got it and is now lying in bed staring at the ceiling and wondering if they’ve got all her sins listed in alphabeti­ cal order up there or as they occurred or in sequence of enormity. On Christmas day I was out of it, which isn’t fair. On my birthday I was out of it, except that two people we didn’t know drove all the way down here from San Francisco to meet me, and so I naturally got out of bed and pretended I was okay. That’s what Churchill would have done, also all the Spartans. They left a couple days later, and I returned to bed. By late January my temp was 102 and then some­ body thought to get me some tetracycline and that lowered it. Mr. Death came by once for me—no kidding; I really saw him—but his little tale that he was beguiling me with petered out fast when Tessa came in the room. Nice-looking guy, though. Very well dressed.
